removed_quadratics.was: for every named-annex hit, find_approver linearly scanned ALL typed members twice, computing flat.char_distance over the full byte gap for each candidate (O(byte distance)), and the «вместе с …» fallback rescanned the whole flattened document for the literal on every hit (O(document bytes)).
removed_quadratics.why_quadratic: link_approved_by runs three times per build_linked_document (the direct pass, inside link_aliases_and_this_refs, and inside build_search_members). The annex-hit count H and the flattened document size both grow with the document, so each call paid O(H x (M + document_bytes)). On the 5514930-byte order H=1784 over a 5.5 MB flattened text, i.e. ~1e10 character comparisons per call, x3 calls.
removed_quadratics.measured_before: analyze 230039 ms of a 234790 ms whole-file run on the 5514930-byte entry (96%); find_approver accumulated 75750 ms of the 77536 ms link_approved_by pass.
removed_quadratics.fix: member_globals (the non-decreasing flattened byte offset of every typed member) is computed once per link_approved_by; the nearest member to the right/left of an annex is one partition_point binary search (O(log M)) instead of a linear scan; the character distance is replaced by chars_between_lt, which counts at most the window bound (450/700) so it is O(window) not O(gap); the single «вместе с» offset is computed once per document, not per annex.
removed_quadratics.behavior_preserving_because: the typed stream is sorted by (block, start) and global_byte is monotone in that order, so member_globals is non-decreasing; the character distance is monotone in the byte gap, so the nearest candidate also has the smallest distance. The linear scans and the boundary lookups therefore select exactly the same candidate, the same window and the same result. No external contract or analyzer semantic changes; npa_analysis_wire.rs is not touched.

measurements.note: release build, M223_S07_TIMING per-stage wall time, one run per entry. 'before' = the pre-analyze-fix binary; published values are from prd/migration/rust-evidence/m223-s07-tokenize-profile.json (T07) and the T08 baseline run; 'after' = the fixed binary.

residual_for_t09.feasibility_estimate: post-fix measured whole-run rates on the largest entries are 3.0-6.5 s/MB; the pinned manifest is 3789431364 bytes over 43785 entries. A linear extrapolation gives a lower bound of a few hours and a single-digit-hour realistic bound including per-entry fixed overhead, versus the pre-fix structural quadratic that made the run infeasible (the 5.5 MB order family alone cost ~240 s per entry). T09 owns the actual full 43785-entry run and its budget decision; this artifact does not claim the run is complete.
